chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it from him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'or what you possess the keys of'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'A man who has a representative managing his wealth, so he eats without his permission.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'or what you possess the keys of' mean in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elucidates the practical application of Surah An-Nur 24:61 by examining the rights of a Wakil (agent) who manages another's wealth. It establishes that while the agent has authority, consuming the principal's assets without explicit permission constitutes a violation of the owner's exclusive right to dispose of their property, reinforcing the Shia legal principle of strict accountability in financial guardianship.
